file.footer: PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, SVG and BMP convert right in your browser via canvas. AVIF, HEIC, TIFF and ICO are handled on the server (Nitro + sharp + WASM) — nothing is stored.

audio.formatsHint: MP3 · WAV · OGG · FLAC · AIFF · CAF · Opus · WebM · M4A · QOA
audio.footer: Audio conversion runs in your browser via a PCM hub: input is decoded with Web Audio (MP3/WAV/OGG/FLAC/AIFF/M4A...) and re-encoded with the audio/encode library to the target format. No ffmpeg, no server — everything works offline.

archive.footer: Archives are unpacked right in your browser: ZIP and GZIP via fflate, TAR via a built-in parser, Brotli via the native DecompressionStream (Chrome 80+, Safari 16.4+). Nothing is uploaded to the server. Click ↓ on any file to download it individually.

audio.title: Audio
audio.description: MP3, WAV, OGG, FLAC, AIFF, CAF, Opus, WebM, M4A, QOA — all in your browser via Web Audio + the audio/encode library.

useless.title: “Useless”

formatsSection.subtitle: Not just the popular formats — UWC is meant to be a “convert anything, into anything” converter: from translit and ROT13 to GeoJSON and vCard.

features.subtitle: No heavy runtimes just for “Hello, World”: every converter runs at the cheapest level where that's possible.

serverless.title: 0 bytes on the server
serverless.text: Text converters are pure functions: they run in the browser, Nitro doesn't even wake up.

nitro.title: Nitro inside
nitro.text: The server side lives in the same Nuxt process: no separate backend and no extra HTTP hop.

stream.title: Streaming, not buffers
stream.text: Large files flow as streams (ReadableStream) instead of landing in memory whole. RAM stays calm.

privacy.title: Files are not stored
privacy.text: Receive → convert → deliver → forget. No persistent storage: private and cheap.

plus.subtitle: The exotic formats program. UWC covers the popular 99% — UWC+ is how the remaining 1% gets in: you request a format, we build it. Free, like everything here.

meta.title: UWC+ — request a format
meta.description: Missing a format? Request it through GitHub Issues: describe the spec, attach an example, get a converter. Free, open-source, no account needed.

free.title: Free forever
free.text: No paywall, no premium tier. UWC+ is a process, not a product: requested formats land in the main converter for everyone.

privacy.title: Privacy first
privacy.text: Your example files are used only to build and test the converter. Nothing is stored — same policy as the whole service.

community.title: Built by demand
community.text: We don't chase formats nobody needs. If you ask, it's real demand — and your issue becomes the spec.

how.title: How it works
how.step1: You open a GitHub Issue with the format description and an example file (template below).
how.step2: We check the spec: is it documented, is there a license-compatible parser, or can it be hand-written.
how.step3: The converter gets built — client-side when possible, server-side for heavy formats.
how.step4: The issue closes with a release note. Your format is now in UWC for everyone.

requirements.title: What a good request looks like
requirements.subtitle: Four things turn «add X pls» into a converter. The first one is mandatory — without it the issue is closed.

spec.title: Format description — required
spec.text: Link the specification, RFC, docs or describe the structure yourself: delimiters, escaping, types. Without this the request cannot be evaluated.

example.title: Example file
example.text: A small real-world sample (or synthetic, if the data is sensitive). This becomes the round-trip test.

direction.title: Conversion direction
direction.text: X → JSON? JSON → X? Both ways? For which target — CSV, YAML, text?

why.title: Use case
why.text: One sentence about where this format comes from. Helps prioritize and pick the right tier (browser vs server).

requirements.rejected: Issues like «add .toon to .json pls» are closed as invalid — without a format description there is nothing to implement. A spec link or your own description is the entry ticket.

examples.title: Issue examples
examples.badWhy: No spec, no example, no direction. Even knowing what TOON is, we'd have to guess the exact dialect, escaping rules and edge cases — that's how broken converters are born.

cta.title: Ready to request?
cta.text: Open a GitHub Issue using the template — copy the good example above and fill in your format. Issues are triaged weekly.
cta.note: Requires a free GitHub account. Issues are public — check existing ones first to avoid duplicates.
